scope: Hyperspectral photometric stereo, hyperspectral LiDAR correction, waveform processing and forest fusion abstract follow-up

records.title: Multispectral Photometric Stereo for Spatially-Varying Spectral Reflectances
records.abstractLevel: CVF公开摘要（会议前版本；与IJCV 2022题名/DOI核对）
records.abstract: Multispectral photometric stereo (MPS) aims at recovering the surface normal of a scene from a single-shot multispectral image, which is an ill-posed problem under common assumptions. This paper shows that the problem becomes well-posed for a surface with uniform chromaticity but spatially varying albedos. If at least three (or two) scene points share the same chromaticity, the formulation uniquely recovers their surface normals and spectral reflectance with four (or five) or more spectral lights. Robust estimation with four or more spectral bands is also discussed. Experiments on synthetic and real-world scenes demonstrate the effectiveness of the formulation.

records.title: EventSpecPS: Photometric Stereo with Multispectral Reflectance Using an Event Camera
records.abstract: Surface geometry and multispectral reflectance estimation are essential for physical scene understanding. Conventional pipelines often require multiple multispectral views or repeated sequential illuminations, which are slow and bandwidth-intensive. EventSpecPS proposes an event-based multispectral photometric stereo system: a Spectrally-Angularly Multiplexed Encoding Device encodes geometric and spectral cues into an event stream, and an Event-based Spectral-Angular Decoder jointly recovers surface normals and absolute multispectral reflectance. This enables single-stage, high-speed, low-bandwidth acquisition and reconstruction while remaining robust to cast shadows and specularities. Experiments on synthetic and real data report state-of-the-art performance; code and data are released.

records.title: An exploration, analysis, and correction of the distance effect on terrestrial hyperspectral LiDAR data
records.abstract: Terrestrial hyperspectral LiDAR (HSL) delivers geographic coordinates and hyperspectral backscattered intensity, but distance effects restrict accurate intensity acquisition and quantitative target retrieval. This study uses homogeneous targets and reflectance panels at different distances to explore the distance effect and proposes a practical piecewise fitting correction model, compared with inverse-distance-square and polynomial models. Vegetation-leaf and 3D-scene experiments show that the distance effect is shared across wavelengths and can be represented by a distance-effect function. The piecewise model achieves the smallest standard deviation, coefficient of variation, and coefficient-of-variation ratio among the tested corrections. For small scanned scenes, incidence-angle effects dominate, so both effects must be considered.

records.title: Assessing hyperspectral LiDAR capability for understory soil spectral retrieval and property estimation
records.abstract: Vegetation canopy limits passive remote sensing of understory soil spectra. This study constructs 3D vegetation-soil scenes from field-measured soil hyperspectral data and customized tree models, then uses the LESS radiative transfer model to simulate hyperspectral LiDAR (HSL) point clouds and hyperspectral imagery under varying vegetation coverage. HSL is evaluated through radiance intensity, spectral curves, and spectral indices. Laser echoes are less affected by canopy multiple scattering than passive imaging; HSL-derived spectral indices are more consistent with reference spectra, with R2 values increasing from below 0.49 for imagery to above 0.83 for HSL. Partial least squares regression using HSL information obtains R2 of 0.332 for soil organic carbon and 0.485 for total nitrogen, demonstrating potential for soil monitoring beneath vegetation.

records.title: Full-waveform hyperspectral LiDAR data decomposition via ranking central locations of natural target echoes (Rclonte) at different wavelengths
records.abstractLevel: 公开论文摘要转录（二级摘要；DOI/出版社页核对）
records.abstract: Hyperspectral LiDAR (HSL) waveforms contain spectral and geometric information, but unstable noise, complex shapes, and wavelength-dependent time delays make conventional single-wavelength decomposition unsuitable. Rclonte (Ranking Central Locations of Natural Target Echoes) introduces rough and refined parameter initialization and re-optimizes ranked central locations across wavelengths to recover weak or overlapping components. Synthetic and measured HSL waveform data show more accurate component and parameter detection, better ranging precision, and spectra superior to Hofton GD and MSWD, with relative neighbor distance error of 0.026–0.085 for measured data. The method is applicable to full-waveform multispectral and hyperspectral LiDAR.

records.title: Urban tree species mapping using hyperspectral and lidar data fusion
records.abstractLevel: 作者公开PDF摘要（正式RSE版本）
records.abstract: This study fuses 3.7 m hyperspectral imagery with 22 pulse/m2 LiDAR at individual crown-object scale to map 29 common tree species in Santa Barbara, California. Watershed segmentation delineates crowns from a canopy maxima model; spectra above an NDVI threshold and 3D LiDAR crown structural metrics are fused and classified with canonical discriminant analysis. Species-level and leaf-type maps reach overall accuracies of 83.4% and 93.5%, respectively, and adding LiDAR improves accuracy by 4.2 percentage points over spectral data alone. LiDAR structure is especially useful for small or morphologically distinctive crowns; the Washingtonia robusta accuracy rises from 29% to 71% with fusion.

records.title: UAV lidar and hyperspectral fusion for forest monitoring in the southwestern USA
records.abstract: This study tests high-resolution LiDAR, hyperspectral, and multispectral UAV data and demonstrates LiDAR–hyperspectral image fusion in treated and control forests and an ecotone in northern Arizona. Fusion reaches 88% overall accuracy, outperforming either data type alone, especially for species with similar spectra but different canopy sizes. LiDAR estimates individual tree height, crown diameter, canopy cover, tree density, and DEM accuracy; structure-from-motion 3D data from multispectral imagery correlates less well with field measurements in dense and structurally complex forests. The sensors and methods support monitoring landscapes undergoing large-scale forest change.

records.title: Fusion of waveform LiDAR data and hyperspectral imagery for land cover classification
records.abstract: Fusion of hyperspectral imagery (HI) and full-waveform LiDAR (FWL) often converts waveforms to discrete returns before merging. This paper preserves waveform shape through a voxelization method that registers FWL to the HI grid and synthesizes waveforms intersecting each voxel column into a superposition waveform. A vertical energy distribution coefficient feature is extracted, and the waveform and HI features are fused for land-cover classification with maximum-likelihood and support-vector-machine classifiers. Experiments show that the synthesized waveforms preserve information from original returns and that joint FWL/HI features improve classification over either data alone or HI combined with discrete LiDAR points.
